query: Deep learning for satellite image change detection

paper.title: NeXt2Former-CD: Efficient Remote Sensing Change Detection with Modern Vision Architectures

summarization.summary: NeXt2Former-CD presents an end-to-end Siamese framework for satellite change detection, utilizing a DINOv3-pretrained ConvNeXt-L encoder with deformable attention to mitigate quadratic self-attention costs while retaining 2D inductive biases. The study reports state-of-the-art performance on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and CDD datasets, achieving F1 scores of 0.955, 0.921, and 0.984 respectively, outperforming Mamba-based baselines despite higher parameter counts. A critical finding is that ConvNeXt-L pre-trained on LVD-1689M significantly outperforms satellite-pretrained ViT variants; however, performance heavily relies on this large auxiliary dataset, limiting direct comparability with models trained on ImageNet or Google Earth. Documented limitations include inference latency exceeding Mamba baselines due to ConvNeXt capacity (18.57 GiB peak VRAM) and training times reaching 19.58 hours. Furthermore, the authors acknowledge that prior literature may have inflated metrics due to interpolation inconsistencies rather than direct computation, and numerical instability excluded certain datasets like DSIFNCD from evaluation.

factual_consistency.reason: Siamese DINOv3-pretrained ConvNeXt-L architecture, deformable fusion, 0.955 WHU-CD/0.921 LEVIR-CD/0.984 CDD F1 results, large pretraining source, 19.58 h training, and 18.57 GiB peak memory are supported. There is a nuance: inference latency is slightly higher than M-CD (36.79 vs 33.84 ms) but explicitly described as comparable, not a major efficiency failure. DSIFN-CD was excluded because the released baseline M-CD training pipeline was unstable, not because NeXt2Former-CD itself was shown to fail.
